FINDING 2 — an unterminated construct is not stopped at the FILE boundary:
it consumes the next module's source. The diagnostic then names an innocent
stdlib/compiler file, and on a big import graph the parse blows the C stack.

(a) WRONG-FILE DIAGNOSTIC
FILE: lex_unterminated_string_bleeds_into_import.zen.txt
CMD:  ./zen check tests/fixtures/zen/fuzz-repro/lex_unterminated_string_bleeds_into_import.zen.txt
OUT:  zenc: ./src/std/core/result.zen:47:19: error[parse]: expected an
        expression, found a token that cannot start one
            prefix := "zen: panic: "
                          ^
      i.e. the compiler blames src/std/core/result.zen line 47 — a perfectly
      well-formed line of the standard library — for a typo in the USER's file,
      and never mentions the user's file at all.
      Column 19 of that line is the `:` INSIDE the literal "zen: panic: ",
      which is the tell: the user's opening `"` was closed by result.zen's
      opening `"`, so the parser resumed INSIDE a stdlib string.
CONTROL: delete the import line and the same file is diagnosed correctly, in
      the right file:  `zenc: <file>:2:6: error[parse]: ...`.
      So the misattribution is caused purely by having ANY import.

(b) STACK BLOWUP FROM THE SAME BLEED
FILE: lex_unterminated_brace_bleeds_into_import.zen.txt  (49 bytes, no
      trailing newline; an unclosed `{` plus one compiler import)
CMD:  ASAN_OPTIONS=detect_leaks=0 ./zen-asan check \
        tests/fixtures/zen/fuzz-repro/lex_unterminated_brace_bleeds_into_import.zen.txt
OUT:  zen: panic: stack overflow (recursion too deep)     (rc 134)
      — and, under load, sometimes instead:
      zen: panic: segmentation fault (invalid memory access)   (rc 134)
      The plain ./zen survives but misattributes to
      ./src/compiler/ast/ast_types.zen:10:9.
CONTROL: with the import replaced by `std.mem.alloc` the ASan build is clean;
      with NO import at all the diagnostic is exactly right:
      `error[parse]: unclosed `{`: expected a matching `}`, found end of input`.

CLASS: (a) wrong diagnostic / cross-file lexer bleed;  (b) crash (stack
       exhaustion) on malformed input, ASan build only.
NOT DEMONSTRATED: a SILENT miscompile. 10 different single-import variants were
       tried; every one still produced an error, just the wrong one.
FOUND BY: reduced from scripts/fuzz-run.sh crash_aa8b702867ba (FUZZ_SEED=424242,
       iteration 885).
